title: task edit diagnoses a REPEATED unknown flag as an arity error, asserting the flag exists
description:
Reported by opum-cli-e2e 2026-09-19 during their TASK-98, against quest 0.9.0. Reproduced here the same day in a scratch workspace against 0.9.0 (the installed binary now matches this repo dev), four cases, before judging.

THE DEFECT. One nonexistent flag produces two contradictory diagnoses depending only on how many times it is passed:

  task edit T-1 --add-ac a --add-ac b   ->  "--add-ac may only be provided once."
  task edit T-1 --add-ac a              ->  "Unrecognized flag --add-ac. Nothing was written: the rest of this command was not applied either. Accepted flags: ..."

The repeated form is the harmful one: "may only be provided once" ASSERTS the flag exists and has an arity constraint, so the caller does what it implies -- retries with one occurrence per call, in a loop. The reporter did exactly that and spent four failed writes before the single-occurrence form revealed the flag was never real. The arity message also makes neither statement the unrecognized-flag message makes: it does not name the accepted set, and it does not say nothing was written, so a caller cannot tell from it whether a partial write occurred.

ROOT CAUSE, verified in src/cli/main.ts rather than inferred. flags() collects arguments with no knowledge of the accepted set -- it receives only repeatableValueFlags -- and throws FlagUsageError at main.ts:419-420 the moment a non-repeatable flag appears twice. An unknown flag is never in the repeatable set, so any repeated unknown flag trips that throw during COLLECTION, before dispatch ever reaches only()/usageFailure (main.ts:484-502), which is the code that knows the allowed list and produces the good message.

SAME ROOT AS QCLI-353, DIFFERENT BRANCH. Both are cases where a failure raised inside flags() pre-empts usageFailure. QCLI-353 is the "return undefined" branch (a flag-shaped positional swallows the argument list); this is the "throw" branch (arity checked before the name is validated). Fixing either does not fix the other. This is the residual gap usageFailure own docblock at main.ts:470-473 already documents, reached by a second trigger.

WHY THE GUESS IS NATURAL, which is what makes this worth fixing rather than documenting. --add-note, --add-label, --add-plan and --add-dependency all exist with exactly the repeated-occurrence shape, so --add-ac is both a natural flag to guess and a natural flag to repeat. QCLI-323 (no append for acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone) is why it does not exist.

NOTE ON QCLI-323: implementing it would make --add-ac real and would MASK this defect without fixing it -- the next guessed-and-repeated flag would diagnose the same way. Fix this independently of QCLI-323.

THE EXIT CODE IS SETTLED: IT IS 2 EVERYWHERE, AND THE REPORTED 1 NEVER EXISTED. The original report recorded exit 1 for both invocations. Measured here at filing time: exit 2, the documented usage code, in every case. opum-cli-e2e then re-measured on their own side against quest 0.9.0 in a real workspace -- four occurrences, two occurrences, one occurrence -- and got exit 2 in all three, confirming there is no divergence between invocation paths and no second defect.

Cause of the wrong number, volunteered by the reporter rather than left as speculation: their loop piped every invocation through jq and never captured the exit status at all, so the 1 was inferred from "usage error, so probably 1" and written beside figures that had been copied from visible output. An earlier revision of this paragraph guessed "most likely a capture artifact on their side", which was close enough to be unhelpful -- the account above is theirs and is the one to keep. Nothing here needs chasing.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE, not a decision. The reporter suggested validating the flag name against the accepted set before the duplicate-occurrence check. That cannot be done inside flags() as it stands: flags() is called at 26 sites and never receives the allowed list, which is applied afterwards at each dispatch site. So the choices are to thread the allowed set into flags(), or to have flags() record a deferred arity violation rather than throwing and let usageFailure decide which message applies -- unrecognized when the offending flag is outside allowed, arity when it is inside. The second keeps the accepted-set knowledge in one place. The reporter, shown both options, endorsed the deferred-violation one and explicitly declined to argue for threading the accepted set through. Choosing between them is this task job.

NOT A DEFECT, recorded so it is not re-reported: --acceptance-criteria rejecting a newline-separated string with "must be a JSON array of strings or {index,text,checked} items" is accurate and actionable. The reporter noted only that the JSON-array requirement is easy to miss when neighbouring flags take plain text, and requested no change.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A repeated flag that is not in the command accepted set is rejected with the unrecognized-flag envelope -- naming the flag, listing the accepted set, and stating that nothing was written -- identical to the message the same flag produces when passed once
A repeated flag that IS in the accepted set and is not repeatable still reports the arity error it reports today, so the fix does not trade one wrong diagnosis for another
A repeatable known flag passed twice still succeeds, verified by asserting the record holds both values rather than by reading the exit code alone
The three cases above are covered by tests that fail against the current parser, demonstrated by running them before the fix rather than asserted
The fix holds for commands other than task edit, since flags() is shared across 26 call sites -- verified on at least one other command with its own accepted set
